target.title: fix(gateway): detach queued-turn abort listener to avoid closure leak (#106654)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`registerQueuedChatTurn` in `src/gateway/chat-queued-turns.ts` attached a `once: true` abort listener whose closure captured the registering `params`/`runId`/`entry`. When the entry was removed by a non-abort path (`completeQueuedChatTurn`, `abortQueuedChatTurnById`, `abortQueuedChatTurns`) or retired as a collect idempotency guard (`retireQueuedChatTurnCancellation`), the listener was never detached. Its closure kept the entry (and the controller reference) alive until the `AbortController` was garbage collected, delaying memory reclamation during intensive restart drains (#106654).

## Why This Change Was Made

A `WeakMap<QueuedChatTurnEntry, () => void>` now holds the listener reference keyed by the entry. Every successful entry removal path (`deleteQueuedChatTurnEntry`) detaches the listener from the signal, and `retireQueuedChatTurnCancellation` detaches it immediately once the entry becomes a permanent idempotency guard. The closure is released as soon as the entry leaves the map instead of waiting for controller GC.

The change is local to the queued-turn registry: no call-site, projection, or protocol behavior changes. Abort-triggered removal still deletes the entry and now also detaches; retired entries still survive abort and are removed only by completion.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Restart/shutdown sequences that cancel many queued turns no longer retain orphaned closures for the controller lifetime, reducing peak memory during drain.

## Evidence

Root cause confirmed on `origin/main` (`0a588fa7952`): `registerQueuedChatTurn` used `params.controller.signal.addEventListener("abort", ...)` with no matching `removeEventListener`.

Regression tests added in `src/gateway/chat-queued-turns.test.ts` verify the listener is detached on complete, retire, and abort-removal:

```
$ node node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/chat-queued-turns.test.ts --no-watch
 RUN  v4.1.10
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  51 passed (51)
   Duration  1.22s
```

New cases (each asserts `signal.removeEventListener` was called with the abort handler, i.e. the closure is released):
- detaches the abort listener when the entry is completed
- detaches the abort listener when a collect entry is retired
- detaches the abort listener after an abort-triggered removal

Local checks: `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` pass on both changed files.

## What was not tested

No full gateway runtime/restart simulation was executed. The fix is confined to listener lifecycle in a pure module; behavior is covered by the vitest suite above. The leak itself (GC delay) is validated indirectly via the detach assertions rather than a heap snapshot.

## Checklist

- [x] Root cause fixed, not symptoms
- [x] Minimal, focused change
- [x] Regression test added
- [x] `oxfmt`/`oxlint` pass
- [x] No AI/automation attribution in commit or body
